prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help find the best short-term rental — but “best” depends on your dates, budget, and what matters most (walking to Broadway vs. quiet yard for kids, near Opry vs. near grocery/restaurants). A few quick questions first:
- What are your travel dates (or month)?  
- Budget per night (or total)?  
- Kids’ ages and any must-have amenities (crib, fenced yard, washer/dryer, parking, elevator, stroller access)?  
- Do you want to be downtown/close to Broadway or prefer quieter neighborhoods/suburbs?

While you decide, here’s a practical guide so you get exactly what a family of four needs.

What to look for (filters/keywords)
- Entire home or apartment; 2+ bedrooms (or 1 large bedroom + sofa bed listed as room for kids).  
- “Family/kid friendly,” “crib/pack ’n play,” “high chair,” “fenced yard.”  
- Washer/dryer and a full kitchen (big time-saver with kids).  
- Free/secure parking if you’ll have a car.  
- Superhost and recent positive reviews (last 6–12 months).  
- Flexible cancellation if your plans might change.  
- Ground-floor or elevator access if you have a stroller or mobility concerns.  

Best neighborhoods by family need
- East Nashville — relaxed, bungalow/house rentals, parks, family-friendly restaurants. Good for a local vibe.  
- 12South & Hillsboro Village — walkable, easy dining/shopping, quieter than downtown.  
- Germantown — charming, newer condos and homes, close to downtown and Bicentennial Mall.  
- The Gulch & Downtown — best if you want to be near Broadway/attractions; expect higher prices and less yard/space.  
- Opryland/Donelson — close to the Grand Ole Opry, outlet mall, and hotels with family amenities; good if you want more suburban space.  
- Franklin (20–30 min south) — historic Main Street, larger houses, great for a quieter family stay or if you want a small-town feel.

Typical property types that work well for a family of four
- 2–3 bedroom bungalow or renovated cottage (East Nashville/12South) — kid-friendly yard and kitchen.  
- 2-bedroom condo with building amenities (Germantown/The Gulch) — pools, elevators, walking distance to eateries.  
- Suburban 3BR house near Opryland — more space and parking, near family attractions.  
- Short-term rental homes near Percy Warner Park for families who like outdoor space.

Price expectations (approximate, seasonal)
- Downtown/Gulch/Germantown: $200–500+/night.  
- East Nashville/12South/Hillsboro Village: $150–350/night.  
- Opryland/Donelson/Franklin: $120–350/night.  
(Prices spike during CMA Fest, major events, and summer weekends.)

Booking tips
- Book early for weekends and festival dates.  
- Read recent reviews for cleanliness, host responsiveness, and whether the listing is accurate.  
- Confirm sleeping arrangements — sometimes couches are listed but not suitable for kids.  
- Factor cleaning fees, service fees, and local occupancy taxes into total cost.  
- Message the host before booking with any questions (crib availability, parking, stroller storage).

If you tell me your dates, budget, and any must-haves (crib, parking, neighborhood preference), I’ll find 3–5 Airbnb/short-term rental options that match and point out the best one for a family of four.
